questions.q: For how many years had Ezekiel been a captive of the Babylonians?
questions.a: Ezekiel had been a captive of the Babylonians for 25 years.

questions.q: How many years ago had the city of Jerusalem been captured?
questions.a: The city of Jerusalem had been captured 14 years ago.

questions.q: To where did God bring Ezekiel in visions?
questions.a: God brought Ezekiel to the land of Israel in visions.

questions.q: What did the man that Ezekiel saw look like, and what was he holding?
questions.a: He looked like a man but shone like bronze, and he was holding a linen rope and a stick for measuring.

questions.q: What was Ezekiel told to report to the house of Israel?
questions.a: Ezekiel was told to report everything that he saw to the house of Israel.

questions.q: In Ezekiel’s vision, what was surrounding the temple complex?
questions.a: In Ezekiel’s vision, a wall surrounded the temple complex.

questions.q: What was the width of the sill of the east gate that the man measured?
questions.a: The sill was one reed wide.

questions.q: How far apart were the alcoves inside the east gate?
questions.a: The alcoves were five cubits apart.

questions.q: How deep was the porch of the east gate, according to the man’s measurement?
questions.a: The porch was eight cubits deep, and its jamb was two cubits.

questions.q: How many alcoves were on the east side of the gate and how did their sizes compare?
questions.a: There were three alcoves on each side and they were all the same size.

questions.q: What did the man measure the width of the gateway entrance to be?
questions.a: The man measured the width of the gateway entrance to be about ten cubits or 5.4 meters.

questions.q: How wide was each alcove in the east gate?
questions.a: Each alcove was six cubits wide.

questions.q: What was the total width of the gate, from one alcove roof to the other?
questions.a: The gate was 25 cubits wide, from one alcove roof to the other.

questions.q: What was the distance from the front of the east gate to the inside end of its porch?
questions.a: The distance from the front of the gatehouse to the end of the porch was 50 cubits or 27 meters.

questions.q: What did Ezekiel see carved on the walls?
questions.a: Ezekiel saw carvings of palm trees on the walls.

questions.q: Where did the man take Ezekiel after measuring in the area of the gate?
questions.a: The man took Ezekiel to the outer courtyard of the temple.

questions.q: How far did the stone pavement extend from each gate?
questions.a: It extended out from each gate as far as each of the gatehouses did.

questions.q: What was the distance between the outer gate and the inner courtyard on the east and north sides?
questions.a: It was 100 cubits or 54 meters between the outer gate and the inner courtyard on the east and north sides.

questions.q: What did the man measure at the gatehouse of the outer wall?
questions.a: He measured its length and its width.

questions.q: How did the measurements of the north gate compare to the measurements of the east gate?
questions.a: They were the same: 50 cubits long and 25 cubits wide.

questions.q: How many steps led up to the north gate?
questions.a: Seven steps led up to it.

questions.q: What led into the inner courtyard?
questions.a: A person had to go through a gate in order to enter the inner courtyard.

questions.q: After measuring the north gate, where did the man lead Ezekiel next?
questions.a: He led Ezekiel to the gate on the south side.

questions.q: What were the length and width of the south gate, as the man measured it?
questions.a: It was 50 cubits long and 25 cubits wide.

questions.q: How many steps led up to the south gate, and what was carved into its jamb?
questions.a: Seven steps led up to it, and palm trees were carved into its jamb, one on each side.

questions.q: What was the distance from the south inner gate to the south outer gate?
questions.a: The distance from the inner gate to the outer gate on the south side was 100 cubits or 54 meters.

questions.q: How did the gates to the inner courtyard compare in size?
questions.a: The gates of the inner courtyard all had the same measurements.

questions.q: How many steps led up to the south gate of the inner courtyard?
questions.a: Eight steps led up to it.

questions.q: After measuring the south gate of the inner courtyard, where did the man take Ezekiel next?
questions.a: He took Ezekiel to the gate on the east side of the inner courtyard.

questions.q: What were the length and width of the east gatehouse of the inner courtyard?
questions.a: It was 50 cubits long and 25 cubits wide.

questions.q: How many steps led up to the east gate of the inner courtyard?
questions.a: Eight steps led up to it.

questions.q: Where did the man take Ezekiel after measuring the east gate of the inner courtyard?
questions.a: He took Ezekiel to the gate on the north side of the inner wall.

questions.q: What were the length and width of the gatehouse on the north side of the inner wall?
questions.a: It was 50 cubits long and 25 cubits wide.

questions.q: How many steps led up to the gatehouse on north side?
questions.a: Eight steps led up to it.

questions.q: For what were the chambers by each of the inner gateways used?
questions.a: The chambers by each of the inner gateways were used to rinse the burnt offerings.

questions.q: What three kinds of offerings did people slaughter on the tables inside the gate’s porch?
questions.a: They slaughtered the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering.

questions.q: How many tables were outside the entrance to the north gate?
questions.a: There were two tables on each side, four tables in total.

questions.q: For what were the four tables on either side of each gate used?
questions.a: The four tables on either side of each gate were used for slaughtering animals.

questions.q: What were the four tables for the burnt offering made of, and what did people place on them?
questions.a: They were made of carved stone, and people placed on them the tools they used to slaughter and prepare the animals for sacrifice.

questions.q: What was placed on the tables besides the tools for slaughtering?
questions.a: The meat for the offering was placed on the tables.

questions.q: What was the chamber that faces south used for?
questions.a: It was for the priests who guarded the temple building.

questions.q: Who was serving as priests in the temple?
questions.a: The descendants of Zadok were serving as priests in the temple.

questions.q: How large was the inner courtyard?
questions.a: The inner courtyard was square, 100 cubits long and 100 cubits wide.

questions.q: What did the man measure after he brought Ezekiel to the porch of the temple house?
questions.a: He measured the jambs of the porch and the width of the gate.

questions.q: What stood on either side of the porch of the temple?
questions.a: Pillars stood on either side of the porch.

commentary.text: Here is a vision, beginning at Ezek. 40, and continued to the end of the book, Ezek. 48, which is justly looked upon to be one of the most difficult portions in all the book of God. When we despair to be satisfied as to any difficulty we meet with, let us bless God that our salvation does not depend upon it, but that things necessary are plain enough; and let us wait till God shall reveal even this unto us. This chapter describes two outward courts of the temple. Whether the personage here mentioned was the Son of God, or a created angel, is not clear. But Christ is both our Altar and our Sacrifice, to whom we must look with faith in all approaches to God; and he is Salvation in the midst of the earth, Ps. 74:12, to be looked unto from all quarters.
